draft.title: Simple interest
card: Simple interest is worked out only on the starting amount, called the principal. The interest is not added to the principal each period, so it never earns interest itself.
The formula is I = Prn. I is the interest, P is the principal, r is the interest rate per period as a decimal, and n is the number of periods.
The rate and the time must use the same unit. A rate of 6% per year needs n in years, so 6 months is n = 0.5.
Example: $2000 at 5% per year for 3 years. I = 2000 × 0.05 × 3 = $300. The total amount after 3 years is $2000 + $300 = $2300.
draft.remember: Simple interest is the same every period, because it is always worked out on the principal.

a.q: Ben invests $4000 at 3% per year simple interest for 2 years. How much interest does he earn?
a.why: I = 4000 × 0.03 × 2 = $240. The $4240 option is the balance after one year only if n were 1 and the interest were added to the principal, but the question asks for the interest alone.
a.clue: Write 3% as a decimal before you multiply.

b.q: Priya borrows $5000 at 8% per year simple interest for 18 months. How much interest does she pay in total?
b.why: The rate is per year, so 18 months is n = 1.5 years. I = 5000 × 0.08 × 1.5 = $600. Using n = 18 gives $7200, which mixes months with a yearly rate.
b.clue: Change the months into years first.

problems.detail: The why misexplains the $4240 distractor. $4240 is the total amount after 2 years (4000 + 240), not the balance after one year. After one year the balance would be 4000 + 120 = $4120.
